---
title: "SC Election Trends Analysis"
format: html
---

```{r}
# load packages and data

library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(stringr)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(tidycensus)
library(ggrepel)


gov_senate_2026_xlsx <- "data/2026_gov_senate.xlsx"

excel_sheets(gov_senate_2026_xlsx)[1:10] # sheet 9 = senate, sheet 2 = governor

```

```{r}
# Separate 2026 senate and gov into 2 dfs

party_names <- c(REP = "Republican", DEM = "Democratic", LIB = "Libertarian",
                 CON = "Constitution", GRN = "Green", UNC = "United Citizens")

# ---- 1. Read both contest sheets into one long table -------------------------
# Each candidate gets a 7-column block (Election Day, Early Voting, Absentee,
# Failsafe, Provisional, Failsafe Provisional, Total Votes). We only keep
# each block's "Total Votes" column.

raw_2026 <- c(senate = "9", governor = "2") |>
  map(\(s) read_excel(gov_senate_2026_xlsx, sheet = s, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
                      .name_repair = "unique_quiet")) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "race") |>
  group_by(race) |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

cells_2026 <- raw_2026 |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("..."), names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(col_num = as.integer(str_remove(col, "...")))  # "...5" -> 5

# Candidate label sits in row 2 (merged across the block), field name in row 3
columns_2026 <- cells_2026 |>
  filter(row %in% 2:3) |>
  select(race, col_num, row, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = row, values_from = value, names_prefix = "row") |>
  arrange(race, col_num) |>
  group_by(race) |>
  fill(row2) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(row3 == "Total Votes") |>
  mutate(
    party_code = str_extract(row2, "^[A-Z]{3}(?= )"),
    party      = party_names[party_code],
    candidate  = str_remove(row2, "^[A-Z]{3} "),
    candidate  = if_else(is.na(party), candidate, str_c(candidate, " (", party, ")"))
  ) |>
  select(race, col_num, candidate, party)


columns_2026   # 5 candidate columns per race, including Write-In

# County names are in column 1 for rows 4 onward; the last row is "Total:"
names_2026 <- cells_2026 |>
  filter(row >= 4, col_num == 1) |>
  select(race, row, county = value)

votes_2026 <- cells_2026 |>
  filter(row >= 4) |>
  inner_join(columns_2026, by = c("race", "col_num")) |>
  left_join(names_2026, by = c("race", "row")) |>
  mutate(
    level  = if_else(county == "Total:", "State", "County"),
    county = if_else(county == "Total:", "South Carolina", county),
    votes  = as.numeric(value)
  ) |>
  select(race, level, county, candidate, party, votes)

# The workbook's own "Total" column (last column), used to QA our sums
xlsx_totals <- cells_2026 |>
  filter(row >= 4, col_num == max(col_num)) |>
  left_join(names_2026, by = c("race", "row")) |>
  mutate(county = if_else(county == "Total:", "South Carolina", county),
         xlsx_total = as.numeric(value)) |>
  select(race, county, xlsx_total)

# ---- 2. Ballots cast and registered voters (Registered Voters sheet) ---------
# The contest sheets have no ballots-cast or over/undervote column, so
# Total Ballots Cast comes from this sheet and Overvotes/Undervotes is derived
# as ballots cast minus votes cast in the race.

registration_2026 <- read_excel(gov_senate_2026_xlsx, sheet = "Registered Voters") |>
  rename(county = County, registered = `Registered Voters`,
         ballots = `Ballots Cast`, turnout_pct = `Voter Turnout`) |>
  mutate(county = if_else(county == "Total:", "South Carolina", county),
         turnout_pct = parse_number(turnout_pct))

# ---- 3. Wide tables in the same layout as the older CSVs ---------------------
# Column order follows the old files: Republican, Democratic, other parties
# (by statewide vote), Write-In last.

candidate_order <- votes_2026 |>
  filter(level == "State") |>
  arrange(race, party != "Republican", party != "Democratic",
          is.na(party), desc(votes))

senate_order   <- candidate_order |> filter(race == "senate")   |> pull(candidate)
governor_order <- candidate_order |> filter(race == "governor") |> pull(candidate)

wide_2026 <- votes_2026 |>
  select(-party) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = candidate, values_from = votes) |>
  left_join(xlsx_totals, by = c("race", "county")) |>
  left_join(select(registration_2026, county, ballots), by = "county") |>
  mutate(`Total Votes Cast`     = xlsx_total,
         `Overvotes/Undervotes` = ballots - xlsx_total,
         `Total Ballots Cast`   = ballots) |>
  arrange(race, level != "State")      # State row first, like the old files

senate_2026 <- wide_2026 |>
  filter(race == "senate") |>
  select(level, county, all_of(senate_order),
         `Total Votes Cast`, `Overvotes/Undervotes`, `Total Ballots Cast`)

governor_2026 <- wide_2026 |>
  filter(race == "governor") |>
  select(level, county, all_of(governor_order),
         `Total Votes Cast`, `Overvotes/Undervotes`, `Total Ballots Cast`)

senate_2026
governor_2026

# ---- 4. QA checks ------------------------------------------------------------

# 46 counties plus one State row in each table
stopifnot(nrow(senate_2026) == 47, nrow(governor_2026) == 47)

# Candidate votes add up to the workbook's Total column in every row
votes_2026 |>
  group_by(race, county) |>
  summarise(sum_of_candidates = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(xlsx_totals, by = c("race", "county")) |>
  filter(sum_of_candidates != xlsx_total)          # expect 0 rows

# County rows add up to the State row
votes_2026 |>
  group_by(race, candidate, level) |>
  summarise(votes = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = votes) |>
  filter(County != State)                          # expect 0 rows

# No county has more votes in a race than ballots cast
bind_rows(senate = senate_2026, governor = governor_2026, .id = "race") |>
  filter(`Overvotes/Undervotes` < 0)               # expect 0 rows

# Registered voters in the contest sheets match the Registered Voters sheet
cells_2026 |>
  filter(row >= 4, col_num == 2) |>
  left_join(names_2026, by = c("race", "row")) |>
  mutate(county = if_else(county == "Total:", "South Carolina", county)) |>
  left_join(registration_2026, by = "county") |>
  filter(as.numeric(value) != registered)        
```

```{r}
# make comparison maps to see shifts in rep/dem leaning across counties in midterms

race_order <- c("2022 Senate", "2022 Governor", "2026 Governor", "2026 Senate")

# read all 4 races into a long table

files <- c(
  "2022 Senate"   = "data/2022_senate.csv",
  "2022 Governor" = "data/2022_gov.csv"
)

raw <- files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "race") |>
  group_by(race) |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

column_labels <- raw |>
  filter(row %in% 1:2) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, X1, X2), names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
  select(race, row, col, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = row, values_from = value, names_prefix = "row") |>
  rename(candidate = row1, party = row2) |>
  filter(!is.na(candidate))

results <- raw |>
  filter(X1 %in% c("State", "County")) |>
  rename(level = X1, county = X2) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, level, county), names_to = "col", values_to = "votes") |>
  inner_join(column_labels, by = c("race", "col")) |>
  mutate(votes = as.numeric(votes)) |>
  select(race, level, county, candidate, party, votes)

# 2026: reshape the cleaned data frames from 01 the same way and stack them on
results_2026 <- bind_rows("2026 Governor" = governor_2026,
                          "2026 Senate"   = senate_2026, .id = "race") |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, level, county), names_to = "candidate",
               values_to = "votes", values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  mutate(party = str_extract(candidate, "(?<=\\()[^)]+(?=\\)$)"))   # "(Democratic)" -> Democratic

results <- bind_rows(results, results_2026)

# 2 party dem share by county

vote_shares <- results |>
  group_by(race, level, county) |>
  summarize(
    dem_votes = sum(votes[party %in% "Democratic"]),
    rep_votes = sum(votes[party %in% "Republican"]),
    total_votes = sum(votes[candidate == "Total Votes Cast"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(dem_share = dem_votes/total_votes, 
         rep_share = rep_votes/total_votes,
         margin = dem_share - rep_share,
         race = factor(race, levels = race_order))

vote_shares |> filter(level=="State")
 

# ---- 3. County shapes and the join -------------------------------------------
# Census cartographic boundary file (generalized, clipped to the shoreline).
# Join on county name after lower-casing and dropping spaces/punctuation,
# so "McCormick" / "Mccormick" or "St. X" style differences can't break it.

sc_counties <- counties(state = "SC", cb = TRUE, year = 2024) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, geometry) |>
  mutate(county_key = str_to_lower(str_remove_all(NAME, "[^A-Za-z]")))

map_data <- vote_shares |>
  filter(level == "County") |>
  mutate(county_key = str_to_lower(str_remove_all(county, "[^A-Za-z]")))

# Any county in the results with no shape (expect 0 rows), and vice versa
anti_join(map_data, st_drop_geometry(sc_counties), by = "county_key")
anti_join(st_drop_geometry(sc_counties), distinct(map_data, county_key), by = "county_key")

map_data <- sc_counties |>
  inner_join(map_data, by = "county_key")

# 46 counties in each of the 4 races
map_data |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(race)
stopifnot(nrow(map_data) == 46 * 4, n_distinct(map_data$GEOID) == 46)

# ---- 4. Maps -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Diverging red-white-blue centered at 50%. The same limits are used on every
# map so a given shade means the same share in every race.

margin_limit <- max(abs(map_data$margin))

share_fill <- scale_fill_gradient2(
  low = "#B2182B", mid = "#F7F7F7", high = "#2166AC", midpoint = 0,
  limits = c(-margin_limit, margin_limit),
  labels = scales::label_percent(style_positive = "plus"),
  name = "Dem share minus\nRep share"
)

# All four races on one page
four_panel <- ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  share_fill +
  facet_wrap(~race, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "South Carolina: Democratic minus Republican vote share by county",
    caption = "Shares are of all votes cast in the race, including third parties and write-ins. 2026 results are unofficial.\nSource: S.C. Election Commission; county boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau (tigris)."
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"),
        legend.position = "right")

four_panel

# One PNG per race
map_2022_senate <- ggplot(filter(map_data, race == "2022 Senate")) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  share_fill +
  labs(title = "2022 U.S. Senate: Scott (R) vs. Matthews (D)",
       caption = "Source: S.C. Election Commission; U.S. Census Bureau.") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

map_2022_governor <- ggplot(filter(map_data, race == "2022 Governor")) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  share_fill +
  labs(title = "2022 Governor: McMaster (R) vs. Cunningham (D)",
       caption = "Source: S.C. Election Commission; U.S. Census Bureau.") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

map_2026_governor <- ggplot(filter(map_data, race == "2026 Governor")) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  share_fill +
  labs(title = "2026 Governor: Wilson (R) vs. Johnson (D)",
       caption = "Unofficial results. Source: S.C. Election Commission; U.S. Census Bureau.") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

map_2026_senate <- ggplot(filter(map_data, race == "2026 Senate")) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = margin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  share_fill +
  labs(title = "2026 U.S. Senate: Graham (R) vs. Andrews (D)",
       caption = "Unofficial results. Source: S.C. Election Commission; U.S. Census Bureau.") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

map_2022_senate
map_2022_governor
map_2026_senate
map_2026_governor
```

```{r}

# summary statistics on voter turnout

race_order <- c("2020 President", "2020 Senate", "2022 Governor", "2022 Senate",
                "2024 President", "2026 Governor", "2026 Senate")

files <- c(
  "2020 President" = "data/2020_pres.csv",
  "2020 Senate"    = "data/2020_senate.csv",
  "2022 Governor"  = "data/2022_gov.csv",
  "2022 Senate"    = "data/2022_senate.csv",
  "2024 President" = "data/2024_pres.csv"
)

# read every race into a very long table

raw <- files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "race") |>
  group_by(race) |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

column_labels <- raw |>
  filter(row == 1) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, X1, X2), names_to = "col", values_to = "candidate") |>
  filter(!is.na(candidate)) |>
  select(race, col, candidate)

results <- raw |>
  filter(X1 %in% c("State", "County")) |>
  rename(level = X1, county = X2) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, level, county), names_to = "col", values_to = "votes") |>
  inner_join(column_labels, by = c("race", "col")) |>
  mutate(votes = as.numeric(votes)) |>
  select(race, level, county, candidate, votes)

results_2026 <- bind_rows("2026 Governor" = governor_2026,
                          "2026 Senate"   = senate_2026, .id = "race") |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, level, county), names_to = "candidate",
               values_to = "votes", values_drop_na = TRUE)

results <- bind_rows(results, results_2026)

totals <- results |>
  filter(candidate %in% c("Total Votes Cast",
                          "Overvotes/Undervotes",
                          "Total Ballots Cast")) |>
  select(race, level, county, candidate, votes) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = candidate, values_from = votes) |>
  rename(votes_cast = `Total Votes Cast`, over_under = `Overvotes/Undervotes`,
         ballots = `Total Ballots Cast`)

# Candidate votes sum to Total Votes Cast
results |>
  filter(!candidate %in% c("Total Votes Cast", "Overvotes/Undervotes", "Total Ballots Cast")) |>
  group_by(race, level, county) |>
  summarise(sum_of_candidates = sum(votes), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(totals, by = c("race", "level", "county")) |>
  filter(sum_of_candidates != votes_cast)

# Votes + over/undervotes = ballots
totals |> filter(votes_cast + over_under != ballots)

# County rows sum to the State row
totals |>
  group_by(race, level) |>
  summarise(ballots = sum(ballots), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = ballots) |>
  filter(County != State)

# Same-year races should report the same ballots cast in each county
totals |>
  mutate(year = str_sub(race, 1, 4)) |>
  group_by(year, county) |>
  summarise(n_values = n_distinct(ballots), min = min(ballots), max = max(ballots),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(n_values > 1)

# turnout summary by race

turnout_by_county <- totals |>
  filter(level == "County") |>
  left_join(select(registration_2026, county, registered), by = "county") |>
  mutate(
    registered    = if_else(str_starts(race, "2026"), registered, NA),
    turnout_rate  = ballots / registered,
    roll_off_rate = over_under / ballots     # ballots that skipped (or spoiled) this race
  )

turnout_summary <- turnout_by_county |>
  group_by(race) |>
  summarise(
    statewide_ballots       = sum(ballots),
    statewide_votes_in_race = sum(votes_cast),
    statewide_roll_off      = sum(over_under) / sum(ballots),
    county_ballots_median   = median(ballots),
    county_ballots_min      = min(ballots),
    county_ballots_max      = max(ballots),
    statewide_registered    = sum(registered),
    statewide_turnout_rate  = sum(ballots) / sum(registered),
    county_turnout_median   = median(turnout_rate),
    county_turnout_min      = min(turnout_rate),
    county_turnout_max      = max(turnout_rate)
  ) |>
  mutate(race = factor(race, levels = race_order)) |>
  arrange(race)

turnout_summary |> print(width = Inf)

# Highest and lowest 2026 turnout counties
turnout_by_county |>
  filter(race == "2026 Senate") |>
  select(county, registered, ballots, turnout_rate) |>
  arrange(desc(turnout_rate)) |>
  slice(c(1:5, 42:46))

# Ballots cast change by county, 2022 -> 2026 (both midterms)
ballots_change <- turnout_by_county |>
  filter(race %in% c("2022 Senate", "2026 Senate")) |>
  mutate(year = str_sub(race, 1, 4)) |>
  select(county, year, ballots) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = ballots, names_prefix = "ballots_") |>
  mutate(pct_change = ballots_2026 / ballots_2022 - 1) |>
  arrange(desc(pct_change))

ballots_change

# statewide ballots cast by race
turnout_chart <- turnout_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = race, y = statewide_ballots)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4A6FA5", width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(statewide_ballots)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "South Carolina: total ballots cast, 2020-2026",
       x = NULL, y = "Ballots cast",
       caption = "2026 results are unofficial. Source: S.C. Election Commission.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

turnout_chart

```

```{r}
# experimenting with data visualizations to tell a story about trends

raw <- files |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, col_names = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "race") |>
  group_by(race) |>
  mutate(row = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

column_labels <- raw |>
  filter(row %in% 1:2) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, X1, X2), names_to = "col", values_to = "value") |>
  select(race, row, col, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = row, values_from = value, names_prefix = "row") |>
  rename(candidate = row1, party = row2) |>
  filter(!is.na(candidate))

results_2022 <- raw |>
  filter(X1 %in% c("State", "County")) |>
  rename(level = X1, county = X2) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, row, level, county), names_to = "col", values_to = "votes") |>
  inner_join(column_labels, by = c("race", "col")) |>
  mutate(votes = as.numeric(votes)) |>
  select(race, level, county, candidate, party, votes)

results_2026 <- bind_rows("2026 Governor" = governor_2026,
                          "2026 Senate"   = senate_2026, .id = "race") |>
  pivot_longer(-c(race, level, county), names_to = "candidate",
               values_to = "votes", values_drop_na = TRUE) |>
  mutate(party = str_extract(candidate, "(?<=\\()[^)]+(?=\\)$)"))   # "(Democratic)" -> Democratic

margins <- bind_rows(results_2022, results_2026) |>
  filter(level == "County") |>
  group_by(race, county) |>
  summarise(
    dem_votes   = sum(votes[party %in% "Democratic"]),
    rep_votes   = sum(votes[party %in% "Republican"]),
    total_votes = sum(votes[candidate == "Total Votes Cast"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(margin = (dem_votes - rep_votes) / total_votes)

# ---- 2. Split and swing, one row per county ----------------------------------

county_shifts <- margins |>
  mutate(race = str_replace(str_to_lower(race), " ", "_")) |>   # "2026 Senate" -> "2026_senate"
  select(county, race, margin) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = race, values_from = margin, names_prefix = "margin_") |>
  left_join(
    margins |> filter(race == "2026 Senate") |> select(county, votes_2026 = total_votes),
    by = "county"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    split        = margin_2026_senate - margin_2026_governor,
    senate_swing = margin_2026_senate - margin_2022_senate,
    gov_swing    = margin_2026_governor - margin_2022_governor
  )

stopifnot(nrow(county_shifts) == 46, !anyNA(county_shifts))

county_shifts |> arrange(desc(split)) |> print(n = 46)

# ---- 3. County context: ACS college share and USDA RUCC ----------------------

# ACS 2019-2023 5-year, table B15003 (educational attainment, population 25+).
# Bachelor's or higher = bachelor's (022) + master's (023) + professional (024)
# + doctorate (025), divided by the table total (001).
acs_education <- get_acs(
  geography = "county", state = "SC", year = 2023, survey = "acs5",
  variables = c(bachelors = "B15003_022", masters = "B15003_023",
                professional = "B15003_024", doctorate = "B15003_025"),
  summary_var = "B15003_001"
)

college <- acs_education |>
  group_by(fips = GEOID, NAME) |>
  summarise(college_share = sum(estimate) / first(summary_est), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(county = str_remove(NAME, " County, South Carolina")) |>
  select(fips, county, college_share)

# USDA ERS 2023 Rural-Urban Continuum Codes, long format:
# FIPS, State, County_Name, Attribute (Population_2020 / RUCC_2023 / Description), Value
# Page: https://www.ers.usda.gov/data-products/rural-urban-continuum-codes
# If the download is blocked, save the CSV to data/raw/ and read it from there.
rucc <- read_csv("https://ers.usda.gov/media/5768/2023-rural-urban-continuum-codes.csv",
                 col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
  filter(State == "SC", Attribute %in% c("RUCC_2023", "Population_2020")) |>
  select(fips = FIPS, Attribute, Value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Attribute, values_from = Value) |>
  transmute(fips, rucc = as.integer(RUCC_2023), pop_2020 = as.numeric(Population_2020))

# Urban / suburban / rural rule
#   rural    = nonmetro county (RUCC 4-9)
#   urban    = metro county (RUCC 1-3) that holds the main city of its own metro
#              area. Edit this list if you draw the line differently.
#   suburban = every other metro county: the ring counties around those cores,
#              plus SC counties in metros centered out of state
#              (Charlotte: York, Lancaster; Augusta: Aiken, Edgefield).
urban_cores <- c(
  "Richland",     # Columbia
  "Charleston",   # Charleston-North Charleston
  "Greenville",   # Greenville-Anderson
  "Spartanburg",  # Spartanburg
  "Horry",        # Myrtle Beach
  "Florence",     # Florence
  "Sumter",       # Sumter
  "Beaufort"      # Hilton Head Island-Bluffton
)

county_context <- college |>
  left_join(rucc, by = "fips") |>
  mutate(
    county_type = case_when(
      rucc >= 4                 ~ "Rural",
      county %in% urban_cores   ~ "Urban",
      TRUE                      ~ "Suburban"
    ),
    county_type = factor(county_type, levels = c("Urban", "Suburban", "Rural"))
  )

# Check: 46 counties, every one has a RUCC code, and the urban list has no typos
stopifnot(nrow(county_context) == 46, !anyNA(county_context$rucc))
setdiff(urban_cores, county_context$county)                     # expect character(0)
county_context |> filter(county %in% urban_cores, rucc >= 4)    # expect 0 rows

county_context |> count(county_type)
county_context |> arrange(county_type, rucc) |> print(n = 46)

analysis <- county_shifts |>
  left_join(county_context, by = "county")

stopifnot(!anyNA(analysis$fips))   # every results county matched a FIPS code

# ---- 4. Summary tables -------------------------------------------------------

# Average swing and split by county type: simple county average, and weighted
# by 2026 Senate votes (closer to what each group contributed statewide)
swing_by_type <- analysis |>
  group_by(county_type) |>
  summarise(
    counties              = n(),
    mean_senate_swing     = mean(senate_swing),
    mean_gov_swing        = mean(gov_swing),
    mean_split            = mean(split),
    weighted_senate_swing = weighted.mean(senate_swing, votes_2026),
    weighted_gov_swing    = weighted.mean(gov_swing, votes_2026),
    weighted_split        = weighted.mean(split, votes_2026),
    total_votes_2026      = sum(votes_2026)
  )

swing_by_type |> print(width = Inf)

# How swing and split track with college share (one row per measure)
analysis |>
  summarise(
    cor_senate_swing = cor(college_share, senate_swing),
    cor_gov_swing    = cor(college_share, gov_swing),
    cor_split        = cor(college_share, split)
  )

senate_swing_model <- lm(senate_swing ~ college_share, data = analysis)
gov_swing_model    <- lm(gov_swing ~ college_share, data = analysis)
split_model        <- lm(split ~ college_share, data = analysis)

summary(senate_swing_model)
summary(gov_swing_model)
summary(split_model)
# Slope reads as: change in margin (in share points) per 1.00 change in college
# share; divide by 10 for "per 10 points of college share".

# ---- 5. Main chart: split-ticket scatter -------------------------------------
# Points above the dashed line: Andrews (D) did better than Johnson (D) there.

label_counties <- analysis |>
  filter(county_type == "Suburban" | rank(desc(abs(split))) <= 5)

split_scatter <- ggplot(analysis, aes(x = margin_2026_governor, y = margin_2026_senate)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey80") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey80") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(size = votes_2026, fill = county_type),
             shape = 21, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text_repel(data = label_counties, aes(label = county),
                  size = 3, min.segment.length = 0, seed = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(style_positive = "plus")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(style_positive = "plus")) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 14, labels = scales::comma, name = "2026 votes") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Urban = "#4A6FA5", Suburban = "#E08E45", Rural = "#7A9A65"),
                    name = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4)),
         size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(fill = "grey60"))) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Senate vs. governor margin by county",
    subtitle = "2026 margin by county (Dem share minus Rep share). Above the dashed line = Senate Democrat did better.",
    x = "Governor margin (Wilson R vs. Johnson D)",
    y = "Senate margin (Graham R vs. Andrews D)",
    caption = "Unofficial results. Source: S.C. Election Commission; USDA ERS 2023 RUCC."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

split_scatter
ggsave("output/split_ticket_scatter.png", split_scatter, width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# ---- 6. Supporting chart: Senate swing vs governor swing, by county ----------

swing_long <- analysis |>
  mutate(county = fct_reorder(county, senate_swing)) |>
  select(county, county_type, senate_swing, gov_swing) |>
  pivot_longer(c(senate_swing, gov_swing), names_to = "race", values_to = "swing") |>
  mutate(race = recode(race, senate_swing = "Senate 2022 to 2026",
                       gov_swing    = "Governor 2022 to 2026"))

swing_dumbbell <- ggplot(swing_long, aes(x = swing, y = county)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_line(aes(group = county), color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(color = race), size = 2.4) +
  facet_grid(county_type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(style_positive = "plus")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Senate 2022 to 2026" = "#2166AC",
                                "Governor 2022 to 2026" = "#9E9AC8"),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(
    title = "Swing toward Democrats, 2022 to 2026, by county",
    subtitle = "Change in margin (Dem share minus Rep share). Right of zero = moved toward the Democrat.",
    x = "Swing in margin", y = NULL,
    caption = "Unofficial 2026 results. Source: S.C. Election Commission; USDA ERS 2023 RUCC."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"),
        legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

swing_dumbbell
ggsave("output/swing_dumbbell.png", swing_dumbbell, width = 8, height = 11, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

# Swing vs college share
swing_college <- analysis |>
  select(county, county_type, college_share, votes_2026, senate_swing, gov_swing) |>
  pivot_longer(c(senate_swing, gov_swing), names_to = "race", values_to = "swing") |>
  mutate(race = recode(race, senate_swing = "Senate swing", gov_swing = "Governor swing")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = college_share, y = swing)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(size = votes_2026, fill = county_type), shape = 21, color = "white", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~race) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(style_positive = "plus")) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 10, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Urban = "#4A6FA5", Suburban = "#E08E45", Rural = "#7A9A65"),
                    name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Swing toward Democrats vs. college share",
       x = "Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher (ACS 2019-2023)",
       y = "Swing in margin, 2022 to 2026",
       caption = "Unofficial 2026 results. Source: S.C. Election Commission; U.S. Census Bureau ACS.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"))

swing_college
ggsave("output/swing_vs_college.png", swing_college, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
